acceptance.check: A Weekly custom report whose To date is a week start shows a summary header ending on that week's true last day, or on today while the week is still in progress. The header never shows the To date itself for a Weekly report whose week has more than one day left in it.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open a Weekly custom report in a window wider than the 'small' breakpoint (512px — tokens.ts:12; the summary header is not rendered at narrow widths, CustomReport.tsx:1063 gates on !isNarrowWidth), and click the calculator icon 'Show Summary' in the topbar (ReportTopbar.tsx:187). Read the header's end date as text. Pick a To date that is a week start at least one full week in the past, so its week has certainly elapsed whatever day QA runs; the header's end date must be the last day of that week (the To date plus six days) and must not be the To date. work_order.approach:
Extract the Weekly end-date rule into one exported getEffectiveEndDate in reportRanges.ts, next to the other range-normalisation helpers, and route all four existing sites plus the two leaky consumers through it. One helper rather than four patches, because the drift between copies is what produced the header bug.

The helper takes balanceTypeOp as well as interval, so the budgeted exclusion lives in the same statement as the widening instead of one clause of the rule being applied and another skipped.

Three of the four sites already compute the value correctly and already call it effectiveEndDate; they only change shape. recalculate.ts changes its input from intervalItem to endDate, which is behaviour-identical: the last element of weekRangeInclusive is weekFromDate(endDate) — _weekRange (months.ts:291-311) pushes week until week equals endWeek = weekFromDate(end), then pushes it again for the inclusive case — and getWeekEnd is d.endOfWeek, so it is idempotent within a week (months.ts:401-409).

Then close the two consumers the rule never reached: custom-spreadsheet.ts:342 passes endDate: effectiveEndDate into setData, and CustomReport.tsx:1074 passes data.endDate to ReportSummary instead of its own raw endDate state. That single setData change makes the header, the totals bar drilldown and the totals row drilldown all agree with the data beneath them, without touching any of those four files — BarGraph.tsx:341, DonutGraph.tsx:513/596/692 and ReportTable.tsx:89/116 all read data.endDate, and ReportTable passes it down to the totals cell at ReportTableRow.tsx:322.

Tests: the helper gets pure unit tests in reportRanges.test.ts covering pass-through, widening, clamp, Monday first-day and budgeted. custom-spreadsheet.test.ts gains assertions that data.endDate matches the final bucket's intervalEndDate. Existing expectations are not touched — they prove the move was behaviour-preserving, so a diff there means the extraction changed something it should not have.

What changed from v4 is one clause of AC-4: the repo-wide 'weekly bucket' grep is rescoped to the four files this change touches, because age-of-money-spreadsheet.test.ts:817 matches the same substring for unrelated reasons and survives. No code and no file list changes.

If the owner prefers a different handle, it is a one-word change in two files.

monthUtils.currentDay() is still hardcoded to '2017-01-01' under global.IS_TESTING (months.ts:172-179), so the new unit tests must mock it with vi.spyOn rather than fake timers, as custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:49-52 already documents.
QA's demo budget has transactions spread over enough weeks for a To date one week back to be offered in the picker. The demo generator anchors to currentDay, so the most recent weeks are populated.

The dashboard path calls the same two spreadsheet factories and therefore inherits the widened bound and the widened drilldown range, but not the header fix — it renders ChooseGraph, not ReportSummary.

No new dependency, and nothing in this plan touches forbidden_paths (.sdlc/**, .github/**, .claude/**, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, migrations, docs/spec/**, .sdlc/memory/**).
work_order.confidence_rationale: Higher than v4 for a narrow reason: the delta between the two plans is one clause of one criterion, and I verified that clause's premise myself by running the exact grep the reviewer cited and reading the fourth hit's surrounding test ('does not generate weekly periods past today', age-of-money-spreadsheet.test.ts:815-822) — it is genuinely unrelated to this rule, so no scoped search can return one hit repo-wide, and rescoping is the only honest fix. I chose the reviewer's second option over the first because 'at most one hit' or a deleted clause would both stop detecting the triplication finding 4 is about, and I explicitly rejected the tempting third option of editing that test file. Because the rejection touched nothing else, I re-derived rather than inherited the rest of v4: all three copies of the rule, the getWeekEnd grep (four hits, so AC-4's first clause is correct as written), ReportSummary's single caller, the two real importers of recalculate.ts, _weekRange and getWeekEnd (which is what makes the intervalItem -> endDate switch behaviour-identical), budgetDataQuery's month keying (which is what makes the budgeted guard meaningful), FilterExpression.tsx:87 passing null (which fixes AC-3's chip wording), and the existing test suite in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:181-292 that acts as the regression net. Two line references in v4 were off by one and I corrected them against the files. Not higher because node_modules is absent in this checkout, so I ran neither the tests, the typechecker, nor the app — every finding is from reading code on main. The two judgement calls that remain, the Shivam-Fl attribution and whether any dashboard caller depended on the previously-widened budgeted bound, are both named in unknowns and each is a one-word change or one follow-up reading to correct.

Council plan (v5). One objection was raised against v4 and it was correct on the facts and correct about the remedy, so v5 changes exactly one clause of one criterion and nothing else. The reviewer offered two ways out — delete the clause, or scope the grep and record the stray match as out of scope — and also named the wrong way: do not add that test file to files[] to make the count come out, because that is the same mistake AC-7 was rejected for last round. Scoping the grep to the four paths this change touches keeps the count exact (three hits on main, one after), which is what makes the clause a real check on the triplication that finding 4 is about; deleting it would have thrown away a true and useful assertion to make the sentence fit. age-of-money-spreadsheet.test.ts is named in out_of_scope with its exact line so nobody 'fixes' it later.

Nothing else moved. The intervalItem -> endDate switch is behaviour-identical: months.ts:291-311 `_weekRange` sets endWeek = weekFromDate(end), loops `while (d.isBefore(_parse(week), _parse(endWeek)))` pushing week, then pushes week once more when inclusive — so the last element of weekRangeInclusive is weekFromDate(endDate). getWeekEnd (months.ts:401-409) is `d.format(_parse(d.endOfWeek(_parse(date), { weekStartsOn: converted })), 'yyyy-MM-dd')`, and endOfWeek of any day in a week is that week's last day, so getWeekEnd(weekFromDate(end)) === getWeekEnd(end).

qa_script: yarn start, and on the welcome screen choose 'Try the demo' (WelcomeScreen.tsx:130) so the budget has transactions.

Use a window wider than 512px throughout. The summary header is not rendered at narrow widths (CustomReport.tsx:1063), the report's totals row is not clickable there either (ReportTableRow.tsx:84), and /accounts renders the narrow AccountsPage, which redirects instead of showing the filter chips.
Go to Reports, open a custom report, set Interval to Weekly, and click the calculator icon ('Show Summary') in the topbar so the header is visible.

Note today's date. Note the start of the current week under the current first-day-of-week setting (Sunday-first by default). Set From to a week start four or five weeks earlier and To to exactly one week before the current week's start — a week start whose week has therefore already fully elapsed, on any run date. (The To pickers only offer week starts: allIntervals is built with weekRangeInclusive at CustomReport.tsx:376-382.)

Assert the header's end date is the last day of the week whose start is the To date you picked — the To date plus six days — and that it is NOT the To date. Worked example: today is Friday 2026-10-02, first day of week is Sunday, current week starts 2026-09-27, so To is 2026-09-20 and the header must end 2026-09-26 (Saturday). The assertion above it is the rule; the example illustrates it.

Set To to the start of the current week. Assert the header's end date is today's date, and is never a date later than today. Worked example: with the same today, To is 2026-09-27 and the header must end 2026-10-02 (Friday), not the week's Saturday 2026-10-03.

Click any bar in the Bar Graph (or the Totals cell of the totals row in the Data Table). The activity list opens on /accounts. Above the transaction table, find the two filter chips whose text begins with the word 'date' — there are exactly two, and the second is the upper bound. Their text as rendered is 'date is greater than or equals <From>' and 'date is less than or equals <end>'. Assert the second one shows the same final-week last day you asserted in step 5, not the To date you picked. Do not look for 'is after or equals' or 'is before or equals': FilterExpression.tsx:87 calls friendlyOp(op, null) without the 'date' type argument, so the accounts page renders the numeric-operator wording instead (util/rule.ts:112/122). The chip row may also carry a category, group, amount or hidden-category chip; ignore every chip that does not begin with 'date'.
Settings > Formatting: set first day of the week to Monday, then reload the report.

RE-PICK To to a Monday week start one week before the current Monday week start. You must pick it again — changing the first day of the week rebuilds the To options (the effect at CustomReport.tsx:425-465 re-runs onSetAllIntervals, which is where weekRangeInclusive at :376-382 applies the new week boundary, while onSetStartAndEndDates only acts when the range is not static) but does not re-snap the stored To date, and the old Sunday date is no longer a valid week start under Monday-first. Worked example: today is Friday 2026-10-02, so the current Monday week starts 2026-09-28, To is 2026-09-21, and the header must end 2026-09-27 (Sunday).
Switch Interval to Daily, Monthly and Yearly with Summary still on; for each, pick a To date from that interval's picker and assert the header's end date is exactly the date you picked.

Confirm the browser console logged no new errors or warnings from the reports screen during the above. (The command-palette DialogTitle warning and the nested-button warning on /reports are pre-existing and out of scope for this ticket — see out_of_scope.)

work_order.root_cause: The Weekly end-date rule is implemented inline in three separate places — custom-spreadsheet.ts:125-128, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:58-61 and recalculate.ts:94-108 — with a fourth consumer at custom-spreadsheet.ts:266. Because there is no single home for the rule, the two consumers that render a date to the user were never given it: ReportSummary is passed the raw endDate from CustomReport.tsx:1074, and setData passes the raw endDate into DataEntity at custom-spreadsheet.ts:342. The header therefore reports the week start while the bucket beneath it runs to the week's true last day. The same triplication is why the rule's own internal guard (balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted', honoured by the date remapping at :147 and :80) is absent from the widening, so the budgeted path is widened while being deliberately excluded from the remap that makes Weekly buckets match.

route_request.reason: This ticket is really several tickets. Findings 1, 4 and 5 are one defect — the Weekly end-date rule is triplicated and never reached the summary header or setData — and are planned here as a single helper-sized fix. Finding 3 (PR #12's title lacks [AI]) is not fixable in this repository: the PR is MERGED and .github/** is a forbidden path. Findings 6 and 7 are pre-existing a11y console errors in the command palette (cmdk Command.Dialog missing a DialogTitle) and the reports dashboard (ReportCard's Button wrapping CalendarCard's month-label Button), unrelated to report date ranges; finding 7's fix is a design call about which of the two buttons survives, not a mechanical edit. This plan therefore covers 1, 2, 4 and 5 and defers 3, 6 and 7 — a maintainer should decide whether to file 6 and 7 as separate issues rather than carry them through implement/review/qa on a report-range bugfix.

work_order.understanding:
v4 was rejected on one count, and it was correct. AC-4's second clause asserted that `grep -rn 'weekly bucket' packages/desktop-client/src` returns exactly one hit, in reportRanges.ts. I re-ran that grep on main: it returns four. Three are the comment carrying this rule (custom-spreadsheet.ts:120, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:55, recalculate.ts:90), and files[] removes all three. The fourth is age-of-money-spreadsheet.test.ts:817 — `// generate weekly buckets through the end of February.` — a comment in the age-of-money clamp test, unrelated to this rule and untouched by files[]. No implementation confined to files[] can make that command return one hit. The reviewer named both ways out: delete the clause, or scope the grep to the files this change touches and record the age-of-money match as out of scope. I take the second, because the clause has real value — it proves the triplicated comment collapses to one copy — and it keeps the benefit without the false claim. Per the same instruction I am NOT adding age-of-money-spreadsheet.test.ts to files[] to make the count come out.

The first half of AC-4 is sound and I kept it verbatim: `grep -rn 'getWeekEnd' packages/desktop-client/src` returns exactly four hits today (custom-spreadsheet.ts:125, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:58, recalculate.ts:97, reportRanges.ts:196). files[] removes three and adds one inside getEffectiveEndDate, so exactly two hits, both in reportRanges.ts, is correct.

That was the only change from v4 — one clause of one criterion. No code in the plan moves. But I re-derived the carried-over plan from source rather than trusting it, and every citation holds: the three copies of the rule are where v4 said (custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:55-61, recalculate.ts:90-108); ReportSummary has exactly one caller (grep over .tsx returns only the import at CustomReport.tsx:50 and the use at :1072); recalculate.ts is imported by exactly two files (custom-spreadsheet.ts:34, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:15) — calendar/crossover/net-worth define same-named locals and are untouched; the drilldown consumers of data.endDate are BarGraph.tsx:341, DonutGraph.tsx:513/596/692 and ReportTable.tsx:89/116; showActivity.ts:56 and :86-93 build the gte/lte pair; budgetDataQuery.ts:210-212 does rangeInclusive(getMonth(startDate), getMonth(endDate)), so the budgeted guard is meaningful; months.ts:172-179 short-circuits currentDay() under IS_TESTING, so the tests must use vi.spyOn; months.ts:291-311 and :401-409 make recalculate's intervalItem -> endDate switch behaviour-identical; FilterExpression.tsx:87 passes friendlyOp(op, null) and util/rule.ts:112/122 gate the date wording on type === 'date', so the rendered chip is 'date is greater than or equals <date>'.

Two line numbers in v4's evidence were slightly off and I corrected them against the file: BarGraph's endDate is at :341 (v4 said :340-341, fine) and ReportTableRow's passthrough is at :322 (v4 said :321-322). Neither changes any instruction to the implementer.
